correctness.rationale: Every odd triple square sum is 3 modulo 4; a triple containing 2 has half-sum 3 modulo 4. A 3-mod-4 prime factor cannot occur inside the triple, by nonresiduosity of -1 modulo that prime. This excludes arbitrary exponent vectors at support 3. Coprimality handles support 2; parity handles odd support 4; the two factorized examples exactly attain bounds 4 and 5. A standard-library verifier independently checks 3654 triples, all n through 300000 and the witnesses; the proof, not the enumeration, establishes infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The referenced full-text prime-power divisibility paper proves existence but not exact minimal support; OEIS A190882 explicitly gives only omega>=3; MathPages proves the related squarefree-only lower bound. The present universal external-prime obstruction for every three-prime exponent pattern implies a strict strengthening and exact even/odd thresholds. value.rationale: The natural sequence A190882 asks which non-prime-powers are divisible by their prime-square sum and reports only an omega>=3 bound. The argument gives the exact uniform lower-bound cutoffs 4 overall and 5 among odd integers, including all exponent patterns, and explains the obstruction with an intrinsic new-prime lemma. This is a motivated sharp structural boundary, not a small numerical increment.
